title: RB-1 — Report Blocks Cutover Delivery
summary: replace singular document report front matter with one validated block-level report host across source, projections, runtime, and dependent services
content_html:
RB-1 — Report Blocks Cutover Delivery

Status And Purpose

RB-1 is proposed and not started. It delivers the complete Report Blocks source-contract cutover: every report-host document moves from viewer_report* front matter to one validated block in its Markdown body, every consumer reads one normalized descriptor, and the browser mounts the report at that exact authored position.

Creating this delivery document does not authorize implementation. When implementation is approved, begin with RB-1.0, record the sanity result in this document, and stop for review before RB-1.1.

The feature contract is settled. RB-1.0 identifies the exact implementation seams and migration footprint; it does not reopen the rejected multiple-instance, parameter, registry, plugin, or capability models already owned by Report Blocks.

Complete Outcome

  • A document contains zero or one report block. Multiple blocks and a mixture of report front matter plus a report block fail source validation.
  • One code-owned parser recognizes the fixed block grammar only in accepted Markdown contexts and returns one normalized document-level descriptor.
  • The descriptor carries registered report identity and the existing closed assignment context: access intent, scope, preset, and sub-scope where applicable.
  • The docs builder emits one inert report host at the block's exact content position plus one normalized payload descriptor. It no longer appends an independently created report root after the document.
  • Public and Manage report composition resolve the descriptor through their existing separate metadata and executable loader allowlists, then mount into that exact generated host.
  • The immutable document doc_id remains the report-host identity.
  • Sub-scope lifecycle, location, publication, deletion, transfer, and other exact-host consumers use the same normalized source owner as the builder rather than reading private front-matter fields or independently scanning Markdown.
  • Every current repository or external-local report-host source is converted in one bounded migration, every affected projection is rebuilt, and active product code contains no compatibility reader or precedence rule for the retired fields.
  • Existing reports retain their report id, access, scope, preset, sub-scope, data authority, public/local composition, route state, and behavior apart from their authored placement.

Current Owners To Inspect

RB-1.0 starts from these ownership seams and narrows the exact changed set before implementation:

  • Docs source parsing, DocRecord, content-token resolution, Markdown rendering, Manage/public metadata projection, and report metadata registry validation;
  • public and Manage document-extras entrypoints, report controllers, executable loader allowlists, and report lifecycle cleanup;
  • sub-scope source creation and host discovery, document-location composition and projection, publish eligibility, deletion follow-through, document transfer, and any other exact report-host readers;
  • complete-source Copy, Import, Review, package, and static-export workflows that could otherwise treat a report block as ordinary transferable prose;
  • every current report-host source across repository and configured external-local scopes, including lifecycle-created docs_subscope hosts;
  • focused builder, service, public-boundary, report-module, sub-scope lifecycle, and route smokes; and
  • Reports, Report Capability and Composition, and Sub-Scope Customisation Architecture as likely durable documentation owners.

This is an inspection route, not a frozen file inventory. RB-1.0 must report exact files, reused seams, estimated production/test footprint, and any workflow whose existing report-host behavior needs an explicit retain, omit, or reject decision.

Delivery Steps

RB-1.0 — Confirm Contract And Cutover Fit

  • [ ] Inventory every active viewer_report* source field, parser, payload writer, browser reader, service reader, source writer, fixture, test, report host, and generated projection.
  • [ ] Fix one exact block syntax, allowed attribute names and values, whitespace and escaping rules, placement rule, ignored Markdown contexts, and errors for malformed, duplicate, mixed-contract, or unknown declarations.
  • [ ] Freeze the normalized in-process descriptor, generated payload shape, inert host markup, public/Manage projection behavior, and exact browser mount/unmount contract.
  • [ ] Confirm how local-only blocks, public-intended but unpromoted reports, and promoted public reports appear in Manage and public document projections without weakening the existing module/data boundary.
  • [ ] Confirm the exact docs_subscope creation, discovery, recorded-host validation, location, publication, deletion, and transfer changes required to preserve current child routes and lifecycle ownership.
  • [ ] Inspect Copy, Import, Review, package, and static-export flows and decide explicitly whether a report block is retained, omitted, rejected, or rendered inert in each existing workflow.
  • [ ] Inventory all current report-host documents and affected scopes, then define the direct source migration and rebuild matrix.
  • [ ] Restate the proposed production files, focused tests, generated products, rough diff size, risks, and rollback boundary before implementation.

Checkpoint: one concise RB-1.0 sanity record confirms the grammar, normalized descriptor, projection and mount flow, source-workflow decisions, exact host migration, implementation footprint, focused evidence, and any unresolved implementation decision. Stop before RB-1.1 implementation approval.

RB-1.1 — Add The Pure Report-Source Contract

  • [ ] Add one shared report-source parser and normalized descriptor owner usable by builders and services without importing browser or management code.
  • [ ] Validate zero-or-one cardinality, the closed attribute vocabulary, registered report/preset/context values, ignored Markdown contexts, exact source ranges, and actionable source-path errors.
  • [ ] Reject mixed report front matter and block source through the new contract while leaving current product readers and current report-host documents unchanged until the atomic cutover.
  • [ ] Add focused pure tests for valid declarations, optional context, malformed syntax, duplicates, unknown values, code/comment examples, and stable normalized output.

Checkpoint: the pure parser and tests pass without changing current report rendering, projections, services, or source documents. Stop before RB-1.2 approval; the tracked product still uses the old contract at this intermediate review gate.

RB-1.2 — Perform The Atomic Product And Source Cutover

  • [ ] Integrate the normalized descriptor into source records, Manage/public payload construction, exact inert-host rendering, and the existing report metadata validation path.
  • [ ] Make public and Manage report composition mount into the generated host, preserve unavailable/error behavior, and release the exact current report through existing navigation and document-generation lifecycle.
  • [ ] Move every direct service consumer and lifecycle-created host writer to the shared report-source owner; no service independently scans raw Markdown or retains a private report-field reader.
  • [ ] Apply the RB-1.0 decisions to Copy, Import, Review, package, and static-export workflows so body placement cannot bypass structural report validation.
  • [ ] Convert every inventoried report-host source to one block, rebuild every affected working/public/search projection, and verify exact report id, access, scope, preset, sub-scope, document identity, and route behavior before and after migration.
  • [ ] Remove the five active viewer_report* source fields, flat payload construction and browser normalization paths, lifecycle template fields, direct service readers, fixtures, and tests that assert the retired contract.
  • [ ] Retain no dual reader, compatibility alias, precedence rule, migration mode, stale generated field, or unconverted active report host when the checkpoint completes.

Checkpoint: all current reports mount at their exact block positions in the intended public or Manage context; all affected services resolve exact hosts through the normalized descriptor; migrated source and generated products contain no active retired fields; focused Python, JavaScript, builder, lifecycle, public-boundary, and report smokes pass. Stop before RB-1.3 closeout approval.

RB-1.3 — Verify And Transfer Durable Ownership

  • [ ] Run the bounded retired-contract scan over production code, active source documents, generated payloads, tests, and configuration, distinguishing deliberate historical documentation from active readers or writers.
  • [ ] Verify every configured report host and the complete public/local report registry-to-loader agreement, including lifecycle-created sub-scope hosts and external-local sources available to the delivery environment.
  • [ ] Run affected scope docs/search dry builds, focused source lint, changed Python/JavaScript lint, the warranted Docs Viewer smoke profile, generated assertions, and git diff --check.
  • [ ] Update Reports with the shipped block source contract, normalized payload and exact-position runtime; update durable sub-scope documentation with normalized host discovery; update Report Capability and Composition only if its durable module boundary actually changed.
  • [ ] Record exact implementation and verification evidence here, prepare the explicit feature/delivery closeout recommendation, and stop for user approval before changing status or retiring any document.

Checkpoint: durable documentation describes the shipped contract, focused and boundary evidence passes, and the closeout list is ready for explicit approval. RB-1 remains open until the user approves closeout.

Focused Evidence Contract

RB-1.0 chooses the smallest exact commands after the changed seams are known. Expected evidence includes:

  • pure parser/normalizer tests for grammar, cardinality, ignored contexts, attributes, registry validation, and normalized descriptors;
  • builder tests for exact placeholder position and projection-specific payload/HTML behavior;
  • service tests for sub-scope creation/discovery, document locations, publish gating, deletion, transfer, and each affected complete-source workflow;
  • JavaScript module tests or smokes proving public/Manage mounting into the existing host, unavailable behavior, navigation cleanup, and absence of a second appended root;
  • a full current-host migration assertion over authoritative sources and generated payloads;
  • focused bin/lint-python and bin/lint-js over changed source, affected scope docs/search builds, the warranted Docs Viewer smoke profile, and git diff --check.

Broad suites are warranted only when RB-1.0 finds a shared source or lifecycle owner whose risk cannot be proved through narrower tests. Browser checks are reserved for exact route/module/mount boundaries rather than ordinary layout or copy review.

Acceptance

RB-1 is complete only when:

  • every active report-host document has exactly one valid report block and no viewer_report* front matter;
  • every non-report document has no report block and emits no report descriptor or host;
  • invalid, duplicate, mixed, and unknown declarations fail with exact source evidence;
  • builders and services consume one normalized source owner, and browsers consume one normalized payload descriptor and exact inert host;
  • reports preserve current public/local availability, data sources, route state, lifecycle behavior, and immutable document host identity;
  • docs_subscope creation, public child reachability, location composition, deletion, transfer, and recorded lifecycle host behavior remain exact;
  • complete-source workflows cannot accidentally turn report configuration into unvalidated prose or executable browser configuration;
  • active source, production code, config, tests, and generated products contain no compatibility reader or stale field contract;
  • durable Reports and sub-scope documentation are current.

Durable Closeout

The primary shipped contract moves into Reports. Exact sub-scope report-host discovery remains in Sub-Scope Customisation Architecture, and Report Capability and Composition continues to own public/local module, data, contribution, and stylesheet separation.

At closeout, Report Blocks should be reviewed for retention as a concise feature rationale or retirement after its stable mental model has been transferred. RB-1 remains as delivery evidence until the user explicitly approves its closeout treatment. Catalogue Works Report Migration becomes eligible for its own sanity checkpoint only after RB-1 is accepted and closed.
